Mulled Wine

Served at: Perchta Day (Perchtenlauf) · Lussinatta (St. Lucia's Vigil)

Serves 6Prep 10 minCook 20 min

Mulled Wine is a warm, spiced red wine traditionally enjoyed during the cold winter months, especially on Perchta Day (Perchtenlauf) and Lussinatta (St. Lucia's Vigil). This festive drink brings warmth and cheer, combining aromatic spices with citrus to create a comforting beverage perfect for holiday celebrations.

Ingredients

  • 1 bottle (750 ml) dry red wine
  • 1/4 cup (50 g) granulated sugar
  • 1 orange, sliced into rounds
  • 1 lemon, sliced into rounds
  • 4 whole cloves
  • 2 cinnamon sticks
  • 3 star anise pods
  • 1/2 teaspoon grated nutmeg
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) brandy (optional)

Method

  1. Pour the red wine into a large pot or saucepan.
  2. Add the sugar, orange slices, lemon slices, cloves, cinnamon sticks, star anise, and grated nutmeg to the pot.
  3. Heat the mixture over medium heat until it is hot but not boiling, stirring occasionally to dissolve the sugar.
  4. Reduce the heat to low and let the wine simmer gently for 15 to 20 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
  5. Remove the pot from heat and stir in the brandy if using.
  6. Strain the mulled wine through a fine mesh sieve to remove the spices and citrus slices.
  7. Serve warm in heatproof glasses or mugs.

Tips

  • Avoid boiling the wine to preserve its flavor and alcohol content.
  • For a non-alcoholic version, substitute red grape juice and omit the brandy.
  • Garnish with a cinnamon stick or a fresh orange slice for a festive presentation.
